content.text: The text reviews gastric dilatation, intestinal indigestion, constipation, enteralgia, and acute/chronic intestinal catarrh. Gastric dilatation arises from pyloric or duodenal stenosis, excessive or fermenting contents, or weakened gastric muscle; symptoms include fullness, delayed vomiting of undigested food, fermentation, constipation, wasting, and characteristic physical signs. Diagnosis relies on vomit analysis, examination, percussion, distension, and stomach-tube findings. Treatment emphasizes diet, rest, and cautious stomach washing, while prognosis depends on the underlying cause. Intestinal disorders reflect impaired digestion, bile, pancreatic, or muscular function, producing gas, pain, altered stools, diarrhea or constipation, malnutrition, and nervous symptoms. Management stresses suitable food, mastication, exercise, hygiene, and treating causes. Travel to cooler seashore or mountain climates, Europe, mineral springs, and hot springs is repeatedly recommended.
